- /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Desktop/fedBuild-manual.md

These are the FED Lead's playbook and build manual for the Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit project (repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa).

Your job: extract a COMPLETE, DEDUPLICATED checklist of every concrete, verifiable requirement or rule these two documents impose on a frontend build/PR. I need to audit six specific commits against them.

For each item, output:
- A short ID (e.g. PB-01 for playbook, BM-01 for manual)
- The exact requirement, stated as something checkable (not vague advice)
- The doc + section/heading it comes from
- Whether it is MANDATORY (must-do, gate) or ADVISORY (should-do, judgement)

Group the output under these headings, and put each item under exactly one:
1. Component/atom completeness (variants, states, all-variants-upfront rules)
2. Testing requirements (which layer, when required, coverage expectations)
3. Storybook requirements (story required, categorisation, play functions)
4. Tokens/styling/CSS structure
5. Accessibility
6. TypeScript/typing
7. Commits, branches, PR hygiene
8. Documentation/comments/annotation of provisional values
9. Verification/V&V process rules (e.g. "prove a design claim before acting", measure-don't-assume)
10. Anything else that doesn't fit above

Be exhaustive but do NOT invent requirements — only what the documents actually state. Where a document states a specific numeric threshold, viewport, token name, or file path, quote it exactly. If the two documents conflict on any point, call that out explicitly in a final section titled CONFLICTS.

Do not audit any code. Only produce the checklist.

The mandate, consolidated 13 14 What the sessions actually assigned you: 15 16 | # | Responsibility | From | 17 |---|---|---| 18 | 1 | Own dependency discovery during refinement | M1 — the strongest expectation raised | 19 | 2 | Protect Salesforce / PWA Kit reuse; challenge "let's build this" | M1 | 20 | 3 | Own component governance — prevent duplicate Buttons, Links, utilities | M1 | 21 | 4 | Strengthen FE PR review criteria | M1 | 22 | 5 | Improve estimation accuracy — surface hidden work before planning | M1 (Jasmijn, repeatedly) | 23 | 6 | Embed accessibility in component stories, not as follow-up | M1 + M2 | 24 | 7 | Follow up design-system gaps with Kiera / design owners | M1 | 25 | 8 | Define the atoms governance model + a refinement checklist | M1 (strategic) | 26 | 9 | Component completeness — all variants designed upfront | M2 | 27 | 10 | Define a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components | M2 | 28 | 11 | Ensure components gracefully handle optional fields | M2 | 29 | 12 | Document accessibility expectations component-by-component | M2 | 30 | 13 | Own page-level validation — visual, responsive, integration, design parity | M2 | 31 | 14 | Push back where requirements are unclear before sizing | M2 | 32 | 15 | Support incremental assembly (build → drop in → verify) | M2 | 33 | 16 | Separate component-build effort from page-composition effort in estimates | M2 | 34 35 **The through-line, in Tim's words:** *"FED leadership needs to identify what already exists before the team commits to building something new."* 36 37 **The one to resist as stated.** #1 makes you a serial gate across both squads' refinement sessions. It won't scale and it will slip. Play 1 handles this by moving the lookup to where the story is drafted and keeping only the judgement calls for yourself. 38 39 ### The quality bar this all serves 40 41 Everything below is calibrated to one number. **The SOW allows no more than 10 defects, and no Sev3.** 42 43 Zimmermann is a luxury brand and is exceptionally particular about UI. That combination means the usual 44 trade — ship it, fix it in QA — is not available here. A visual defect that would be a shrug on another 45 project consumes part of a very small budget. 46 47 Three consequences to plan around rather than discover: 48 49 - **Vigilance is the job, not an overhead on the job.** Be as vigilant as possible, on every PR. 50 - **Budget real time for checking.** A proper pass over a UI PR — preview environment, Figma, tokens, 51 states, responsive — is **an hour or more**. Treat that as the cost of the review, not as slippage. 52 - **Do as much as we can and flag the rest.** Where design is missing, ambiguous or contradictory, the 53 answer is to raise it, not to invent a value. An invented value becomes a defect *and* a design-system 54 divergence. 55 56 --- 57 58 ## 2. Your operating rhythm 59 60 Sixteen responsibilities, four moments. Everything below hangs off this. 61 62 | When | Plays | Time | 63 |---|---|---| 64 | **Story drafting** (BA-initiated, async) | 1 — reuse & dependency check | Async, minutes per story | 65 | **Refinement** (per story) | 1, 3, 9, 14 — dependencies, variants, push-back | In the session | 66 | **Pre-sprint-planning** (weekly) | 2 — estimation validation | ~30 min | 67 | **PR review** (continuous) | 5 — the human-only checks | Per PR | 68 | **Design review** (weekly, with Kiera) | 6 — design-system gaps | Standing slot | 69 70 Two standing items that don't fit a cadence: the **renderer contract** (Play 4, once per Contentful component) and **page-level validation** (Play 7, once per page assembly). 71 72 --- 73 74 ## Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check 75 76 *Covers responsibilities 1, 2, 3, 8* 77 78 ### The ladder (agreed in M1) 79 80 ``` 81 Salesforce / PWA Kit capability 82 ↓ (nothing fits) 83 Existing shared component in overrides/ 84 ↓ (nothing fits) 85 Existing pattern 86 ↓ (nothing fits) 87 New implementation ← justify this out loud 88 ``` 89 90 ### Where to actually look 91 92 | Question | Source | 93 |---|---| 94 | Does a Base, Override or Custom component already exist? | `.claude/registry/components.md` — columns: **Origin · Path · Props · Tier · Squad · Consumers**. Regenerated automatically by the pre-commit hook on any `overrides/app/**` change | 95 | Same for hooks / utils / pages / routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` | 96 | What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and `/app/hooks/` | 97 | Is it already claimed by a squad? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squadA.md` | 98 | What tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier` | 99 100 The `Origin` column is doing most of the work: **`Base` means it exists but isn't scaffolded into `overrides/` yet** — which is a cost, not a free win (see below). 101 102 ### Worked examples, already verified 103 104 | Ask | What already exists | 105 |---|---| 106 | Size selector | Base `swatch-group/` — index, swatch, plus an existing test | 107 | Add to bag | Base `product-view/index.jsx` — already does `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the button and label, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling, and an `updateCart` variant | 108 | Max purchase quantity | Base `quantity-picker/` | 109 | Variant resolution | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` | 110 111 Worth knowing before SFCC-650 is sized: its description says *"Cart API integration is in scope"*, but the base already performs the cart call. That story should read as **extend `product-view`**, not build cart integration. 112 113 ### Override-first — why the second rung is where the value is 114 115 The ladder says "reuse before build". The stronger version, and the one to hold the line on: 116 **default to overriding the base component, not writing a new one.** 117 118 The reason is not tidiness — it's that an override **inherits the wiring for free**. Override 119 `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart modal, bundle 120 handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of those has to be 121 re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed, and none of it is visible in the story points. 122 123 There's a second-order effect worth naming in refinement. PWA Kit's resolver rewires imports 124 transparently, so **overriding a component SFCC's own base components already import means the whole base 125 template inherits your version** — no call sites touched. A bespoke component in a new folder reaches only 126 the pages someone remembers to wire it into. Same visual result on the page you're building; very 127 different coverage across the site. 128 129 ⚠️ **One documented exception: `shared/ui/`.** That directory is consumed through a barrel 130 (`shared/ui/index.jsx`), and the barrel's own re-exports are **relative** (`export {Button} from 131 './Button'`). The `ccExtensibility` resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` 132 specifiers, so a relative import inside `node_modules` is never redirected. **208 base files import 133 that barrel; none import `shared/ui/Button` directly — so overriding `shared/ui//` intercepts 134 nothing.** It is a place to put raw Zimmermann primitives for *our own* code to import explicitly, not 135 an interception point. See "Two component families" below. 136 137 So the question in review isn't only "did you reuse?" but **"is this an override, and if not, why not?"** 138 139 **In flight, and relevant:** Han is extending the registry generator to account for the `shared/` folder 140 as well, and is building the override-first approach into the F2R workflow — so the default lands in the 141 tooling rather than depending on everyone remembering it. Worth tracking; it removes work from Play 1. 142 143 ### The hidden cost to name every time 144 145 If `Origin = Base`, the component isn't in `overrides/` yet, and AGENTS.md's **Copy-first rule** applies before any functional work: 146 147 1. Copy base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` 148 2. Convert to TypeScript, fix imports 149 3. `npx tsc --noEmit` 150 4. Add a temporary `console.log` marker 151 5. **Stop — a human confirms the override renders instead of the base** 152 6. Then build; remove markers 153 154 It's serialised and human-gated. **The first story against a given base component pays it; later ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't — exactly Jasmijn's concern. Either split it into an enabler story or size the first story accordingly. 155 156 ### Making this scale (the fix for #1) 157 158 Add one line to the BA prompt template in Confluence 274137093: 159 160 > *"Check `.claude/registry/components.md` — does a Base, Override or Custom component already cover this? Report Origin, Tier, Squad and Consumer count."* 161 162 That makes four of the six refinement questions self-service. You keep the two that need judgement: 163 164 - **Is extending the base the right call, or is a Zimmermann-specific build justified?** 165 - **Is the design-system prerequisite real, or can we proceed?** 166 167 ### Preventing duplicate atoms (#3, #8) 168 169 The atoms question — *"when does an atom deserve its own story?"* — is largely already answered by existing convention rather than needing a new model: 170 171 - A story is required for anything **exported from its folder** under `overrides/app/components/` or `/pages/`. 172 - **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants via the parent's stories. 173 - The Storybook categorisation (`Foundation / Elements / Layout / Commerce / Forms / Pages / Contentful`) gives you the vocabulary: `Elements/` *is* the atoms layer. 174 175 Applied to 04.7's `↳ Sub-component` rows: Pause/Play, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons don't each need a story unless independently reusable. Without that rule the Footer alone generates four. 176 177 ### The atoms governance model — decided (closes #8) 178 179 Three developers independently inferred three different answers from the same rules file, so this is now 180 written down. Both halves are settled; the developer-facing version is in the FED Build Manual §3. 181 182 **Where they live, and what they're called** 183 184 ``` 185 overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}//index.tsx 186 ``` 187 188 **camelCase, one folder per component.** These are Zimmermann-authored, so `conventions.md`'s default 189 applies; the kebab-case rule is scoped to files *mirroring a base Salesforce file*, and no 190 `@salesforce/…/zimm-button` exists to mirror. It also satisfies `components.md`'s named-export-matches-folder 191 rule. Precedents: `pageContainer/`, `pdpProductInfo/`. 192 193 Three casings coexist and each is right in its own family — worth stating in review, because generalising 194 from one to another is the mistake people make: 195 196 | Family | Casing | Why | 197 |---|---|---| 198 | SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Upstream imports that exact path | 199 | ui-kit component | **`zimmButton/` camelCase** | Zimmermann-authored — the default | 200 | `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream's own casing | 201 202 **Tiering** is by what the component's own template renders — atom renders nothing, molecule renders only 203 atoms, organism renders at least one molecule. An icon passed as a prop doesn't count; slotted children 204 don't count. Tier follows composition, not pixel size. The F2R contract already records this as 205 `composes: [...]` and machine-checks it in `02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs`, so **use the contract's 206 tier rather than re-deriving it in refinement.** 207 208 **The styling surface: a theme recipe, always.** 209 210 | Case | Surface | 211 |---|---| 212 | It **is** a Chakra component | `theme/components/.ts` recipe; `variant`/`size` resolve automatically | 213 | **Bespoke multipart** Zimmermann component | Recipe + register + `useMultiStyleConfig` + `chakra()` factory | 214 | Static, non-interactive, heavily reused | `.zimm-*` class in `globalStyles.ts` | 215 | Nothing else fits | `sx`, then co-located `.scss` — last resort | 216 217 `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` is the worked example for the bespoke case. The `chakra()` factory is 218 what makes it possible to style a native element from a recipe — that was the missing piece people kept 219 hitting. 220 221 **The argument to use when someone proposes co-located CSS instead** (and it will come up, because plain 222 CSS handles `:hover` perfectly well): a stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`, which is *derived output*. 223 Authoring there forfeits `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive 224 arrays and the 125 drift-guard tests. It's not bad CSS — it's the wrong end of the token pipeline. 225 226 --- 227 228 ## Play 2 — Estimation validation 229 230 *Covers responsibilities 5, 16* 231 232 Run this before sprint planning, not in it. 233 234 ### The re-baseline to communicate once 235 236 M2 concluded pages become assemblies. The honest consequence: 237 238 - **Homepage / page estimates should go down.** Composition genuinely is cheaper. 239 - **Component estimates should go up by more than the pages save.** 240 241 Because a component story now carries: all variants upfront + accessibility AC + a mandatory Storybook story + a test where logic-heavy + Copy-first scaffolding on first touch. 242 243 If only the first half of that lands, the programme will look like it got faster and won't have. Say this out loud in planning — once, clearly. 244 245 ### Split the two kinds of effort (#16) 246 247 | Component build | Page composition | 248 |---|---| 249 | Real frontend development | Assembly and configuration | 250 | Variants, states, accessibility | Integration testing | 251 | Storybook + tests | Visual validation | 252 | Sized as build work | Sized as validation work | 253 254 Don't let them be estimated with the same scale. 255 256 ### Challenge list 257 258 For each story before it's sized: 259 260 - [ ] `Origin = Base`? → Copy-first cost is in, or split out 261 - [ ] All variants captured, or only the ones on the first page? 262 - [ ] Accessibility written as AC, or assumed? 263 - [ ] Storybook story accounted for? 264 - [ ] Designs confirmed, or still in progress? (04.7 status column) 265 - [ ] Does it depend on anything in Play 8's open list? 266 - [ ] Composition variant hiding as a configuration variant? (Play 3) 267 268 --- 269 270 ## Play 3 — Component completeness & variant review 271 272 *Covers responsibilities 9, 11* 273 274 M2's rule: a component isn't complete until it covers all supported variants, and the page just configures it. One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one. 275 276 ### The distinction to hold 277 278 | Kind | Examples | How it's built | 279 |---|---|---| 280 | **Configuration variant** | text alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off, body copy present/absent | Props on one component ✅ Tim's rule applies directly | 281 | **Composition variant** | 1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up grids | A **container/slot component** — structurally a second component | 282 283 This matters because a composition variant priced as a prop will be under-estimated. On the Studio Experiences path especially, a repeating structure can't be a prop — the composition primitive is `children`. So "one Editorial Card with all variants" often resolves to *two* components: the card, plus a container holding one or two. 284 285 Better outcome — the container is reusable anywhere — but it changes the count. Catch it at refinement. 286 287 ### Why "upfront" is a hard requirement here, not a preference 288 289 The Contentful sync is **additive-only — it cannot delete a field from a published content type**. Getting the variant model wrong isn't rework, it's semi-permanent. This is the strongest argument you have for holding the line on variant completeness, and it supports Tim's position rather than fighting it. 290 291 ### Optional-field handling (#11) 292 293 M2: don't assume CMS fields are populated. Every Contentful-backed component needs AC for the absent case — no empty space, no placeholder, no layout break. Make it a standing question in refinement rather than a per-story discovery. 294 295 --- 296 297 ## Play 4 — The renderer contract 298 299 *Covers responsibility 10* 300 301 M2 asked for "a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components." This is the artifact that makes the Contentful story and the PWA Kit story independently workable — without it they drift, and additive-only sync makes drift expensive. 302 303 **The requirement it satisfies:** `02-contentful.md` §2 — *"TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time."* 304 305 **The artifact:** one table, identical in both stories of every Contentful pair. 306 307 | Field ID | Display name | Type / control | Required | Localised | Notes | 308 |---|---|---|---|---|---| 309 | `image` | Image | Media | Yes | No | | 310 | `imageAlt` | Image Alt Text | shortText | No | Yes | behaviour when empty — see Play 6 | 311 | `bodyCopy` | Body Copy | longText | No | Yes | | 312 | `ctaLabel` | CTA Label | shortText | No | Yes | CTA renders only if label **and** URL set | 313 | `ctaUrl` | CTA URL | shortText | No | No | internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` | 314 315 **Field IDs, not display names.** "Body copy" in prose is where drift starts. 316 317 **You own the template; the BA fills it; you sign off the field IDs before the Contentful story is built.** That signature is the cheapest possible insurance against an undeletable wrong field. 318 319 **Note for the ordering question:** for Studio Experiences components the contract is generated from the React props rather than authored first — so the review point moves to the component's prop type. Which pattern a given component uses is still unresolved (Play 8). 320 321 --- 322 323 ## Play 5 — PR review 324 325 *Covers responsibility 4* 326 327 The useful move here is knowing what the tooling already catches, so your attention goes where it's actually needed. 328 329 ### Already mechanical — don't spend review time on it 330 331 | Check | Enforced by | 332 |---|---| 333 | Missing `alt` on `` | ast-grep `img-missing-alt` | 334 | `IconButton` without `aria-label` | ast-grep `icon-button-missing-aria-label` | 335 | `onClick` on non-interactive element without `role` | ast-grep `clickable-non-interactive-element` | 336 | Payment credentials logged | semgrep `payment-credential-logged` | 337 | Unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | semgrep `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` | 338 | Type errors, lint, conventional commits | `tsc --noEmit`, lint, commit-msg hook | 339 | Registry freshness | pre-commit hook | 340 341 ### Not enforced — this is your list 342 343 | Gap | Why it matters | 344 |---|---| 345 | **Hardcoded hex / px values** in Chakra props and `.scss` | `css.md` states plainly it isn't mechanically enforced. Highest-frequency design-system violation | 346 | **Component complexity / size** | No `complexity` or `max-lines-per-function` in `.eslintrc.js` — confirmed | 347 | **Chakra `` without alt** | The ast-grep rule matches lowercase `` only. Every Contentful component here uses `` — so the guard doesn't cover the component family under discussion | 348 | **Duplication / reuse** | No tool detects "this is a second Button". This is the core of responsibility #3 and it is entirely human | 349 | **Salesforce alignment** | Whether base capability was leveraged — judgement only | 350 351 Two of these are cheap to close, and the repo's own rules files already recommend the fix: an ast-grep rule for hardcoded design values, and the two ESLint core rules. **Both touch Tier 1 files** — raise as a decision, don't land quietly. See §Guardrails. 352 353 ### Gate zero — does it actually build? 354 355 **Check this before spending review attention on anything else.** A PR has already been opened on this 356 project with a failing typecheck — missing type declarations that the branch itself had previously 357 supplied and lost in a merge. Reviewing the design of code that doesn't compile wastes the expensive part 358 of your day. 359 360 ```bash 361 npx tsc --noEmit # must be clean 362 npm run lint # separate real errors from auto-fixable prettier noise 363 npx vitest run 364 ``` 365 366 Two things worth knowing about this failure mode, because it will recur: 367 368 - **A merge can silently delete a declaration.** When a branch merges `develop` and both sides touched the 369 same ambient-types file, the merge can resolve to develop's version and drop what the branch added. It 370 typechecks on neither side's intent and nobody notices until CI or a local build. 371 - **It isn't always the author's mistake.** In that instance a second error came from following a repo 372 rules file that named a package which doesn't exist on the installed Storybook major. Check whether the 373 rule or the code is wrong before raising it as a code finding. 374 375 Make "green locally before opening" the expectation, and say so once to the whole team rather than 376 per-PR. It isn't about blame — it's that the review budget is an hour per PR and this spends it on nothing. 377 378 ### Review across three surfaces, not one 379 380 Reading the diff is the smallest part. For any UI PR, look at all three: 381 382 | Surface | What only it will tell you | 383 |---|---| 384 | **The diff** | Tokens vs literals, reuse vs reimplementation, abstractions respected | 385 | **The preview environment** | What it actually renders — states, responsive behaviour, whether hover/focus work at all | 386 | **Figma** | Whether the rendered output matches the design, and which gaps are design gaps rather than build gaps | 387 388 Every `feature/*` and `fix/*` branch now auto-deploys to its own MRT environment and posts the URL on the 389 PR. There is no longer a reason to review a UI change from the diff alone — **open the environment and put 390 it beside Figma.** If no URL comment appeared, the branch had no open PR when it was pushed; a further 391 push once the PR exists will post it. 392 393 Evaluate the rendered output against Figma deliberately, at the breakpoints the design defines. Anything 394 that doesn't line up is either a build finding or a design gap — and separating those two is your call, 395 not the developer's. 396 397 ### Tokens and CSS — the highest-yield thing you check 398 399 This is where divergence starts, it is not mechanically enforced, and both PRs currently in flight have 400 drifted in different directions. Be deliberately vigilant here. 401 402 `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` is the authority. The hierarchy, in order: 403 404 1. `textStyle` for anything textual — **never** a raw `fontSize` 405 2. Semantic token strings — `color="text.default"`, `padding="m"` 406 3. The component's own `theme/components/.ts` for variant / size / state 407 4. `sx` only for a genuine prop-system gap 408 5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` truly can't express it 409 410 What to actively look for: 411 412 - **The correct token, not just a token.** A value that resolves to the right pixels via the wrong token 413 passes a casual glance and breaks the moment the design system moves. Two `sx` blocks recently 414 hand-rebuilt what `textStyle="heading3"` and `textStyle="body2"` already provide, property for property. 415 - **`var(--zimm-*)` in the right layer.** It is the convention *inside* `theme/components/*.ts`. In 416 component JSX it is not — that's rungs 1 and 2. Seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` is a signal to look closer. 417 - **`--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases in JSX.** They exist only for the `.zimm-*` global classes. The 418 named scale (`m`, `l`, `xl`) is the Chakra-facing surface. 419 - **A theme recipe that nothing consumes.** A `theme/components/.ts` file that is written and 420 registered but never read via `useStyleConfig` looks like compliance and is dead code. 421 - **A second copy of the token registry.** Any new utility that re-types token names as strings 422 reintroduces exactly the drift the derived-token work removed. 423 - **Interaction states in JavaScript.** `useState` for hover / press / focus instead of 424 `_hover` / `_active` / `_focusVisible` means those states are dead until hydration, sticky on touch, 425 and unreachable by the theme. 426 427 ### Tests and stories — the minimum, while UI is the focus 428 429 The build focus is UI, and that's fine — but don't let coverage reach zero on the way through: 430 431 - **Unit tests where they earn their place** — data mapping, transforms, non-obvious logic. Not for 432 re-exports or passthroughs. 433 - **At minimum, scaffold the Storybook story.** Every component exported from its folder needs one. A 434 scaffolded story with a `Default` export and the meaningful states is the floor, even if the `play` 435 function comes later. It's also the surface your own review depends on. 436 437 ### Review questions, in order 438 439 0. **Does it build?** `tsc`, lint, tests — gate zero above 440 1. Was an existing component / hook / utility reused, or is this a second implementation? 441 2. **Is it an override, or a bespoke build — and if bespoke, why?** 442 3. Are all design values tokens — and the *correct* tokens, in the correct layer? 443 4. Does it respect existing abstractions, or work around them? 444 5. Was base Salesforce capability leveraged where it exists? 445 6. Accessibility: keyboard, focus order, states — beyond what ast-grep catches 446 7. Storybook story present? Test where logic-heavy? 447 8. **Does the preview environment match Figma at the defined breakpoints?** 448 9. **For a ui-kit component: right folder, right casing, right styling surface?** 449 `components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}//index.tsx`, styled by a recipe. A 450 `.styles.ts`, a `cssVars`-style helper, a new `.zimm-*` class, or inline styles all mean the same 451 conversation — see "The atoms governance model" in Play 1. 452 453 --- 454 455 ## Play 5b — Verifying a design claim before you act on it 456 457 *Learned the expensive way on the footer build. Four times a conclusion reversed once the source was 458 actually read, and each reversal would have shipped a wrong change.* 459 460 ### Absence in an extracted spec is not a decision 461 462 `f2r/02-design/specs/` files carry `` and a `Status: draft` 463 header. They are **mechanical dumps of a Figma node**, not rulings. When the text-input spec had no 464 `clearable` attribute, that meant the Figma component doesn't have one — not that the design system had 465 ruled one out. Treating it as a ruling nearly deleted a control rather than making it opt-in. 466 467 Same trap in the other direction: the spec *did* define `trailing-icon`, which settled a question two 468 code comments had recorded backwards. 469 470 ### A value in the codebase is not a spec until you find its source 471 472 `header.ts` carried `width: min(597px, 60vw)` with a comment deriving 597 from 70 and the aspect ratio. 473 Grepping `overrides/` and `.docs/` for `597` returned three hits: the definition, its own comment, and one 474 copy. **No Figma node, no ticket, nothing.** A "fix" to make the header logo honour that value would have 475 been shipping a number nobody had ever approved. 476 477 Contrast the icon geometry: `327px`/`39px` cite Figma nodes in their comment, and the nodes check out. 478 479 **The test:** can you name the node or the doc? If not, it's a guess someone typed, however confident the 480 surrounding comment sounds. 481 482 ### Ask for the node. It costs the designer thirty seconds. 483 484 Four times on this build the answer came from reading a Figma node directly — the chevron geometry, the 485 four chevron rotations, the site-map item heights, the subscribe heading binding. Each took one message. 486 Each replaced a derivation I would otherwise have defended with arithmetic. 487 488 Deriving is legitimate when the source *shows* the derivation — all four chevrons export an identical 489 path, so Figma itself is rotating one glyph, and reproducing that is reading, not guessing. Deriving from 490 "it's probably the same as the other one" is not. 491 492 ### An audit that matches on value alone will produce confident nonsense 493 494 A style-mirror check flagged three constants as duplicating existing tokens. All three were false: 495 496 | Flagged | Why it was wrong | 497 |---|---| 498 | `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` ≡ `--zimm-scale-1200` | The token is **48px**. Swapping would have broken WCAG 1.4.4 — px doesn't scale with zoom | 499 | `SIZE_COL_NAV = '8.75rem'` ≡ `--zimm-scale-3500` | Same — the token is 140px | 500 | `SIZE_MODAL_SUB = '30rem'` ≡ `breakpoints.sm` | Coincidence. A modal width has no relationship to a breakpoint | 501 502 The checker normalised units and ignored semantic role. Two of the three "fixes" would have been 503 regressions. **Before acting on a tooling finding, confirm the thing it matched is the thing it means.** 504 505 ### A grep count is not a coverage verdict 506 507 A prop-vs-story audit reported `trailing` as having "zero story coverage", and I reported it as a gap. It 508 was covered — by three `play` functions in the molecule that fills the slot, which is the correct level 509 for a slot prop. The same audit missed a story that *does* test a clear button, because the story matches 510 on `/clear input/i` and the grep was case-sensitive on the aria-label. 511 512 Both errors have one shape: **a proxy reported as the finding.** When a check returns zero, establish 513 which zero it is — untested, tested elsewhere, or unused. 514 515 ### A passing test can be encoding the bug 516 517 Phase 3 asserted `contact icons are not focusable` — green for weeks. The icons weren't focusable because 518 the hrefs were never wired through; the assertion had frozen a defect as expected behaviour. Wiring them 519 correctly turned the suite red. 520 521 Worth a standing question in review: *would this test still pass if the feature were broken in the 522 obvious way?* 523 524 --- 525 526 ## Play 6 — Accessibility 527 528 *Covers responsibilities 6, 12* 529 530 M1 and M2 both landed on accessibility living **inside** component stories, as AC, not as a follow-up task. 531 532 ### The per-component AC set (#12) 533 534 Standing list to apply to every component story: 535 536 - Keyboard operability and reachability 537 - Focus order and visible focus states 538 - Interaction states (hover, active, disabled, focused) 539 - Screen-reader behaviour for images and icon-only controls 540 - Behaviour when optional content is absent 541 542 **Baseline is WCAG 2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible *and* the reason is documented. file.content: # FED Lead Playbook **Derived from:** the two "Contentful v PWA Kit Components and User Story Alignment" sessions **Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 **Companions:** [fedBuild-manual.md](./fedBuild-manual.md) (the developer-facing half — how to build) · [componentStories-BA-guide.md](./componentStories-BA-guide.md) (the BA-facing version) · [pr52-pr55-findings.md](./pr52-pr55-findings.md) (worked example of Play 5 applied to two live PRs) · `.docs/temp/{componentStoryReview,meeting2Prep,meeting2Analysis}.md` (the underlying analysis) **Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` in-repo — if this playbook and that file disagree, it wins. Purpose: the two sessions put sixteen things on your desk without saying when or how any of them get done. This turns that into a rhythm, a set of repeatable plays, and the specific mechanics for each. --- ## 1. The mandate, consolidated What the sessions actually assigned you: | # | Responsibility | From | |---|---|---| | 1 | Own dependency discovery during refinement | M1 — the strongest expectation raised | | 2 | Protect Salesforce / PWA Kit reuse; challenge "let's build this" | M1 | | 3 | Own component governance — prevent duplicate Buttons, Links, utilities | M1 | | 4 | Strengthen FE PR review criteria | M1 | | 5 | Improve estimation accuracy — surface hidden work before planning | M1 (Jasmijn, repeatedly) | | 6 | Embed accessibility in component stories, not as follow-up | M1 + M2 | | 7 | Follow up design-system gaps with Kiera / design owners | M1 | | 8 | Define the atoms governance model + a refinement checklist | M1 (strategic) | | 9 | Component completeness — all variants designed upfront | M2 | | 10 | Define a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components | M2 | | 11 | Ensure components gracefully handle optional fields | M2 | | 12 | Document accessibility expectations component-by-component | M2 | | 13 | Own page-level validation — visual, responsive, integration, design parity | M2 | | 14 | Push back where requirements are unclear before sizing | M2 | | 15 | Support incremental assembly (build → drop in → verify) | M2 | | 16 | Separate component-build effort from page-composition effort in estimates | M2 | **The through-line, in Tim's words:** *"FED leadership needs to identify what already exists before the team commits to building something new."* **The one to resist as stated.** #1 makes you a serial gate across both squads' refinement sessions. It won't scale and it will slip. Play 1 handles this by moving the lookup to where the story is drafted and keeping only the judgement calls for yourself. ### The quality bar this all serves Everything below is calibrated to one number. **The SOW allows no more than 10 defects, and no Sev3.** Zimmermann is a luxury brand and is exceptionally particular about UI. That combination means the usual trade — ship it, fix it in QA — is not available here. A visual defect that would be a shrug on another project consumes part of a very small budget. Three consequences to plan around rather than discover: - **Vigilance is the job, not an overhead on the job.** Be as vigilant as possible, on every PR. - **Budget real time for checking.** A proper pass over a UI PR — preview environment, Figma, tokens, states, responsive — is **an hour or more**. Treat that as the cost of the review, not as slippage. - **Do as much as we can and flag the rest.** Where design is missing, ambiguous or contradictory, the answer is to raise it, not to invent a value. An invented value becomes a defect *and* a design-system divergence. --- ## 2. Your operating rhythm Sixteen responsibilities, four moments. Everything below hangs off this. | When | Plays | Time | |---|---|---| | **Story drafting** (BA-initiated, async) | 1 — reuse & dependency check | Async, minutes per story | | **Refinement** (per story) | 1, 3, 9, 14 — dependencies, variants, push-back | In the session | | **Pre-sprint-planning** (weekly) | 2 — estimation validation | ~30 min | | **PR review** (continuous) | 5 — the human-only checks | Per PR | | **Design review** (weekly, with Kiera) | 6 — design-system gaps | Standing slot | Two standing items that don't fit a cadence: the **renderer contract** (Play 4, once per Contentful component) and **page-level validation** (Play 7, once per page assembly). --- ## Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check *Covers responsibilities 1, 2, 3, 8* ### The ladder (agreed in M1) ``` Salesforce / PWA Kit capability ↓ (nothing fits) Existing shared component in overrides/ ↓ (nothing fits) Existing pattern ↓ (nothing fits) New implementation ← justify this out loud ``` ### Where to actually look | Question | Source | |---|---| | Does a Base, Override or Custom component already exist? | `.claude/registry/components.md` — columns: **Origin · Path · Props · Tier · Squad · Consumers**. Regenerated automatically by the pre-commit hook on any `overrides/app/**` change | | Same for hooks / utils / pages / routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` | | What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and `/app/hooks/` | | Is it already claimed by a squad? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squadA.md` | | What tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier` | The `Origin` column is doing most of the work: **`Base` means it exists but isn't scaffolded into `overrides/` yet** — which is a cost, not a free win (see below). ### Worked examples, already verified | Ask | What already exists | |---|---| | Size selector | Base `swatch-group/` — index, swatch, plus an existing test | | Add to bag | Base `product-view/index.jsx` — already does `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the button and label, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling, and an `updateCart` variant | | Max purchase quantity | Base `quantity-picker/` | | Variant resolution | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` | Worth knowing before SFCC-650 is sized: its description says *"Cart API integration is in scope"*, but the base already performs the cart call. That story should read as **extend `product-view`**, not build cart integration. ### Override-first — why the second rung is where the value is The ladder says "reuse before build". The stronger version, and the one to hold the line on: **default to overriding the base component, not writing a new one.** The reason is not tidiness — it's that an override **inherits the wiring for free**. Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of those has to be re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed, and none of it is visible in the story points. There's a second-order effect worth naming in refinement. PWA Kit's resolver rewires imports transparently, so **overriding a component SFCC's own base components already import means the whole base template inherits your version** — no call sites touched. A bespoke component in a new folder reaches only the pages someone remembers to wire it into. Same visual result on the page you're building; very different coverage across the site. ⚠️ **One documented exception: `shared/ui/`.** That directory is consumed through a barrel (`shared/ui/index.jsx`), and the barrel's own re-exports are **relative** (`export {Button} from './Button'`). The `ccExtensibility` resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` specifiers, so a relative import inside `node_modules` is never redirected. **208 base files import that barrel; none import `shared/ui/Button` directly — so overriding `shared/ui//` intercepts nothing.** It is a place to put raw Zimmermann primitives for *our own* code to import explicitly, not an interception point. See "Two component families" below. So the question in review isn't only "did you reuse?" but **"is this an override, and if not, why not?"** **In flight, and relevant:** Han is extending the registry generator to account for the `shared/` folder as well, and is building the override-first approach into the F2R workflow — so the default lands in the tooling rather than depending on everyone remembering it. Worth tracking; it removes work from Play 1. ### The hidden cost to name every time If `Origin = Base`, the component isn't in `overrides/` yet, and AGENTS.md's **Copy-first rule** applies before any functional work: 1. Copy base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` 2. Convert to TypeScript, fix imports 3. `npx tsc --noEmit` 4. Add a temporary `console.log` marker 5. **Stop — a human confirms the override renders instead of the base** 6. Then build; remove markers It's serialised and human-gated. **The first story against a given base component pays it; later ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't — exactly Jasmijn's concern. Either split it into an enabler story or size the first story accordingly. ### Making this scale (the fix for #1) Add one line to the BA prompt template in Confluence 274137093: > *"Check `.claude/registry/components.md` — does a Base, Override or Custom component already cover this? Report Origin, Tier, Squad and Consumer count."* That makes four of the six refinement questions self-service. You keep the two that need judgement: - **Is extending the base the right call, or is a Zimmermann-specific build justified?** - **Is the design-system prerequisite real, or can we proceed?** ### Preventing duplicate atoms (#3, #8) The atoms question — *"when does an atom deserve its own story?"* — is largely already answered by existing convention rather than needing a new model: - A story is required for anything **exported from its folder** under `overrides/app/components/` or `/pages/`. - **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants via the parent's stories. - The Storybook categorisation (`Foundation / Elements / Layout / Commerce / Forms / Pages / Contentful`) gives you the vocabulary: `Elements/` *is* the atoms layer. Applied to 04.7's `↳ Sub-component` rows: Pause/Play, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons don't each need a story unless independently reusable. Without that rule the Footer alone generates four. ### The atoms governance model — decided (closes #8) Three developers independently inferred three different answers from the same rules file, so this is now written down. Both halves are settled; the developer-facing version is in the FED Build Manual §3. **Where they live, and what they're called** ``` overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}//index.tsx ``` **camelCase, one folder per component.** These are Zimmermann-authored, so `conventions.md`'s default applies; the kebab-case rule is scoped to files *mirroring a base Salesforce file*, and no `@salesforce/…/zimm-button` exists to mirror. It also satisfies `components.md`'s named-export-matches-folder rule. Precedents: `pageContainer/`, `pdpProductInfo/`. Three casings coexist and each is right in its own family — worth stating in review, because generalising from one to another is the mistake people make: | Family | Casing | Why | |---|---|---| | SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Upstream imports that exact path | | ui-kit component | **`zimmButton/` camelCase** | Zimmermann-authored — the default | | `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream's own casing | **Tiering** is by what the component's own template renders — atom renders nothing, molecule renders only atoms, organism renders at least one molecule. An icon passed as a prop doesn't count; slotted children don't count. Tier follows composition, not pixel size.
